According to reports, Apple's annual sales in India surpassed US$10 billion for the first time in the last fiscal year.

In a country where the per capita annual income is less than US$3,000, this achievement is particularly impressive—especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the U.S....

For many years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But in recent years, with the growth of the local economy and the company finally being able to open Apple Stores locally, the situation has changed dramatically.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given India's low per capita income and the fact that iPhones are actually manufactured there, you might expect local pricing to be much lower than in the U.S. In reality, however, due to high taxes, Apple products are priced higher in India than in the U.S.

Apple has tried to offset this gap to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently, about one in four iPhones is manufactured in India, but most of them are shipped to the U.S. for sale. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements to avoid U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports.
